initial_reasons.AGNES: She is composed and alert, attending to the hawk while registering the unfamiliar man nearby.
initial_reasons.WILL: He is drawn to Agnes but uncertain how to approach, trying to appear at ease.

AGNES.reason: She turns her attention fully to him and offers a measured greeting.
Hearing that he is the Latin tutor, she briefly considers what she has already heard about him.
She lightly teases him to ease the awkwardness while making clear that she expects an answer.
She corrects him calmly but firmly, asserting the distinction with quiet confidence.

WILL.reason: Her direct question makes him more self-conscious as he searches for a satisfactory answer.
The knowledge that she has heard of him heightens his uncertainty.
Her pointed question unsettles him, and he momentarily searches inward for an explanation.
His hesitation becomes visible as he falters under her scrutiny.
He gathers himself and re-engages with her, trying to shape a plausible explanation.
Another hesitation exposes how difficult it is for him to speak naturally in her presence.
Mentioning the bird gives him a safer subject, and his attention settles on the hawk.
